answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock stake subject to cryptographic stake burning with superlinear cost scaling: registering n identities requires burning tokens proportional to O(n^2), imposing heavy economic friction. An attacker attempting to turn a peaceful meadow of nodes into a compromised willow network faces quadratic loss, while cryptographic proofs bind each identity as indelibly as sable ink to prevent multi-identity arbitrage.
